rounds.text: Saumya Consultants Ltd is heavily discounted against its underlying asset base, trading at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.57x with a share price of ₹ 105 against a book value of ₹ 184 [E2], and a P/B of 0.55x compared to the sector benchmark of 1.26x [E7]. The company is operating virtually debt-free [E42] with a conservative non-current liability to equity structure [E30] and pristine short-term liquidity supported by a current ratio of 123.07x [E31]. Crucially, operational momentum is undergoing a powerful inflection, demonstrated by trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth surging by 60% [E17], compounded profit growth accelerating by 120% [E18], and net profit up 59% year-on-year [E50]. This earnings acceleration is starkly disconnecting from stale sentiment [E56], as the stock currently languishes near the bottom at just 8% of its 52-week range [E5]. Promoters have steadfastly maintained their 54.88% stake, signaling rock-solid internal alignment through the cycle [E33]. Conceded: the company carries a near-term negative return on equity of -3.8% [E13] and negative operating cash flows of ₹ -8.48 Cr for Mar 2026 [E28], alongside historical top-line contractions over three and five-year windows [E15, E16].

Saumya Consultants Ltd carries severe fundamental and valuation risks that are entirely unsupported by its current market price of ₹ 105 [E2, E35]. Despite a low-looking price-to-book ratio, the business destroys shareholder capital, demonstrated by a negative return on capital employed of -10.01% [E10] and a negative return on equity of -4% last year [E26]. Top-line erosion is severe and secular, with compounded sales growth contracting by -18% over 5 years and -20% over 3 years [E15, E16]. Furthermore, operations are actively bleeding cash, evidenced by a deeply negative operating and free cash flow of Rs -8.48 Cr in March 2026 alongside ballooning working capital days that have blown out from 544 days to 1,156 days [E28, E29, E48]. Valuation metrics equally disconnect from reality, as the stock trades at an expensive P/E of 48 alongside a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of only Rs 49 per share, representing a staggering margin of safety of -113.2% [E1, E35, E36]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong short-term profit metrics including a 120% jump in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a comfortable short-term current ratio [E18, E31].

Conceded: [E35] regarding the DCF intrinsic value and [E28] regarding the negative operating cash flow in March 2026. However, the bear's focus on historical contraction ignores massive recent acceleration, evidenced by trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 60% and compounded profit growth of 120% [E17, E18]. Conceded: [E10] regarding historical ROCE, yet the company is almost debt-free, has reduced debt, and boasts a comfortable current ratio of 123.07x alongside pristine balance sheet safety [E30, E31, E41, E42]. Furthermore, the stock trades at an attractive 0.57x price-to-book value against a book value of ₹ 184, sitting near the bottom of its 52-week range at just 8% of the way up [E2, E5, E43]. Conceded: [E48] on working capital days, but profits are growing faster than 1-year price growth by 155% in a price-led setup that shows the market is only starting to catch up to accelerating fundamentals [E39, E52].

Conceded: [E17, E18] regarding the trailing twelve-month acceleration in sales and profit growth. However, that short-term burst does nothing to excuse a multi-year top-line collapse featuring a 5-year sales contraction of 18% and a 3-year contraction of 20% [E15, E16]. The bull leans on a pristine balance sheet and a low price-to-book ratio of 0.57x [E2, E30, E31], but ignores that a low valuation multiple is entirely justified by a negative return on capital employed of 10.01% [E10] and a median 3-year return on equity of just 8% [E25]. Furthermore, pointing to the bottom of the 52-week range at 8% [E5] does not signal a discount when working capital days have bloated from 544 days to an alarming 1,156 days [E48]. That massive capital lockup directly explains why operating cash flow collapsed to negative ₹ 8.48 crores in March 2026 [E28], turning the bull's asset-safety narrative into a capital-efficiency trap.
